adds.title: Executive Order on public employment discrimination - Gov. Steve Beshear June 2008
adds.summary: On June 2, 2008, Kentucky prohibited hiring or firing state employees based on sexual orientation or gender identity, restoring protections first issued in 2003 and removed in 2006 that had allowed dismissal simply for being gay or transgender.

adds.title: EEOC v. R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes - U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
adds.summary: On March 7, 2018, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit covering Kentucky held in EEOC v. R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes that Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibits firing an employee for being transgender or transitioning because it penalizes failure to conform to birth-assigned sex stereotypes and necessarily takes sex into account, and that the Religious Freedom Restoration Act does not permit a private employer to fire a transgender worker on religious belief that sex is immutable God-given sex, after funeral director Aimee Stephens was fired in 2013 for disclosing her planned transition.
